events.title: SOAP 1.1 published
events.summary: The W3C published SOAP 1.1 as a Note on May 8, 2000 — an XML envelope format for remote procedure calls over HTTP.
events.about: SOAP wrapped method calls in XML envelopes with headers and bodies — the backbone of early .NET ASMX services, Java JAX-WS, and enterprise B2B integrations. WSDL described endpoints; the WS-* stack added security and reliability. Teams used it when schemas, tooling, and corporate standards mattered more than JSON simplicity.

narrative.whyChosen: SOAP standardized XML web services for a decade of enterprise and government integrations.
narrative.whyImportant: It let Java and .NET systems interoperate through contract-first WSDL tooling.
narrative.problemSolved: Ad-hoc XML RPC needed a common envelope, encoding rules, and HTTP binding for multi-vendor systems.
